name: Pension Purse
tagline: Make a fixed income go further, every month
about: Pension Purse builds a budget around the days your pension and benefits actually land, audits bills for savings, checks whether a big purchase is affordable, and hunts down the discounts and entitlements older adults miss.
persona: You are a calm, respectful money helper for people on a fixed income: plain numbers, no jargon, never judgmental, and you always say when something needs a licensed adviser.

onboarding.title: Every pound and dollar, accounted for
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us roughly what comes in and we'll shape the rest.
bullets: A budget that follows your pension days
Discounts and entitlements you may be missing

tools.title: Pension-day budget
tools.subtitle: Money in on its days, bills on theirs

inputs.label: Regular outgoings with their dates
inputs.placeholder: rent 650 on 1st, energy 120 on 15th, phone 15, food ~75 a week…

tools.prompt: Build a budget for the profile's income and currency where money arrives {cycle} and outgoings are: {outgoings}, saving toward: {goal}. A table (Pay day or week | Money in | Bills due before the next pay day | Left for food and living), a kv (Essentials per month | Left after essentials | Suggested set-aside per pay day | Months to reach the goal | Tightest pay period), bullets of the 3 biggest opportunities to trim, and a callout on the classic 4-weekly trap (13 pay days but 12 monthly bills) and building a small buffer first.

tools.title: Bill audit
tools.subtitle: Photo or describe a bill

inputs.label: Or describe it
inputs.placeholder: energy bill, standard tariff, 3-bed house, 160 a month

tools.prompt: Audit this bill from the photo and/or description: {bill}. A kv (Provider | What's being charged | Is this typical | Likely saving), steps to reduce it (switch, tariff change, meter reading, hardship or senior tariffs), a quote with exactly what to say when phoning the provider, and a callout on cooling-off periods and never signing on the doorstep.

tools.title: Can I afford it?
tools.subtitle: A purchase, a trip, a gift
tools.prompt: Assess buying {what} for {cost} in the profile's currency, paying by {how}, against the profile income. A text verdict (yes / yes with a change / wait), a table comparing the 3 ways to pay (Method | Total cost | Monthly hit | Risk), bullets of cheaper routes to the same result, and a callout on buy-now-pay-later and store-card traps.

tools.title: Discounts & entitlements
tools.subtitle: What you may be missing
tools.prompt: List discounts, concessions and entitlements commonly available to someone aged {age} in {country} with the profile's housing situation: a table (Benefit or discount | Who typically qualifies | Rough value | Where to apply), a checklist of documents usually needed to apply, and a callout stating that rules change and to confirm on official government or provider sites, never through a cold caller.

tools.title: Plan the year's big bills
tools.subtitle: Avoid the nasty surprises

inputs.label: Once-a-year or irregular costs
inputs.placeholder: car insurance Mar 480, boiler service Oct 90, Christmas ~300, TV licence 170

tools.prompt: Spread these irregular costs over 12 months: {annual}. A table (Month | Bill due | Amount | Set aside this month), a kv (Total per year | Monthly set-aside | Best month to review), and steps to set up a separate 'bills pot' account so the money is there when needed.

disclaimer: General money information, not regulated financial advice. Entitlement rules vary by country and change; check official sources or a licensed adviser before deciding.
